title: seeded-telemetry-for-pin-decisions-and-expiring-verification
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When publishing Redwood-verified performance profiles we lack a lightweight, production-seeded telemetry signal to decide whether a model version should be pinned, refreshed, or auto-expired. This leads to conservative pinning, manual refresh cycles, and occasional customer regressions during canaries.

Goal: Define and implement a seeded telemetry feed and an expiration policy that ties into the profile publish pipeline. The telemetry should drive automatic 'staleness' flags, recommended pin windows, and an expiration trigger that moves profiles into a 'review required' state rather than silently removing them. This ticket coordinates the PM spec, engineering acceptance criteria, and the staged rollback/simulation harness to validate behavior prior to GA.

Scope: (a) telemetry design (signals, sampling frequency, normalization for region/hardware), (b) publish-time metadata fields for profiles (seeded_sample_size, baseline_cost_fingerprint, expiry_ttl_days), (c) automatic staleness scoring and UI indicators in Console, (d) integration with canary/rollback simulator for pin expiration scenarios.

Out of scope: full automated republish; manual steward signoff flows remain unchanged for this iteration.
acceptance_criteria: A telemetry schema is published (Confluence) and approved by Eng and SRE
Publish artifacts include seeded_sample_size and cost_fingerprint metadata on performance profiles
Profiles with expired telemetry move to 'Review Required' and generate audit log entries
Console shows a staleness score and a one-click 'request-refresh' action
Canary simulator reproduces at least three expiry/rollback scenarios in staging with pass/fail metrics
tasks: PM: finalize telemetry signal list and normalization rules
Eng: implement sampling and ingestion pipeline (internal telemetry topic)
Eng: augment profile publish API to accept seeded metadata and expiry TTL
Console: add staleness indicator, tooltip copy, and request-refresh action
QA: create regression tests for expired profile behavior and canary simulator scenarios
SRE: define alert thresholds for sudden profile degradation post-publish
progress_updates: 2026-02-18 - Kickoff: aligned on goals with Eng (Marco), SRE (Lina), Console (Jared). Decided seeded telemetry will start at 1% sampling of production traffic for newly onboarded profiles.
2026-02-25 - PM spec draft published: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROF/Seeded+Telemetry+Spec. Requested feedback from Eng and SRE.

2026-03-03 - Eng design review: agreed to normalize latency and CPU cost by regional baseline; store cost_fingerprint as a hashed proto in profile metadata. Action: ENG to prototype ingestion connector (ENG-77221).
2026-03-08 - Console mocks reviewed: staleness score UI v1 accepted; added request-refresh audit event requirement. Design feedback added to ticket DES-20444.
2026-03-12 - Staging POC: small end-to-end flow validated with synthetic traffic. Canary simulator ran two expiration scenarios; one timing edge-case found and filed as ENG-77298.
decisions: Seed sampling starts at 1% for the first 14 days after profile publish, then downsamples to 0.1% until expiry TTL
Expiry behavior moves profile to 'Review Required' instead of automatic unpublish to preserve auditability
Cost fingerprint will be a normalized 64-bit hash, stored in profile metadata for drift detection only (not human-readable cost metrics)
Initial staleness scoring combines sampled latency p95 delta, throughput drop, and cost-fingerprint divergence with weighted factors (0.5, 0.3, 0.2)
Rollback simulator will be parameterized with region, hardware tier, and traffic mix to validate expiry-triggered fallbacks
risks: Sampling too low may not surface regressions on low-traffic models
Incorrect normalization could cause false positives in staleness scoring across regions
Storing cost fingerprints introduces privacy/PII review surface if linked to billing — confirmed as hashed but needs legal signoff
Automated expiry could create support churn if not surfaced clearly in Console
